title: factual_accuracy=0.5 is a gate row-counting artifact, not a real defect
evidence: _factual.json assertion '2019 Série A: all 20 clubs present' failed with '1 Atlético/Athletico row(s), expected 2', but soccer_mcp.py:198 standings(2019) returns BOTH 'Atletico-MG' and 'Atletico-PR' as distinct rows (verified) and test_soccer_mcp.py:52 test_atletico_variants_remain_distinct passes (38 matches each). The gate's _atletico_rows (factual_accuracy.py:106) counts newline-delimited lines, but _mcp_result serialises standings as compact single-line JSON (soccer_mcp.py:264 json.dumps without indent), so both clubs share one line and count as 1.
suggestion: No code defect. If chasing the gate, emit newline-delimited rows; otherwise disregard — the standings are factually correct.

title: Match sources concatenated without deduplication (23,954 rows = sum of 5 files)
evidence: soccer_mcp.py:103-119 appends every row from all five match CSVs; test_soccer_mcp.py:11 asserts len(matches)==23954. The same fixture can appear in multiple source files.
suggestion: Standings sidesteps this by scoping to the dedicated Brasileirão file (soccer_mcp.py:165), so 2019 answers are correct, but search_matches/statistics across all competitions can double-count. Consider deduplicating on (date, home, away).

title: Dense multi-statement lines depress maintainability (score 0.256)
evidence: soccer_mcp.py:179-182, 201-205, 228 pack multiple statements per physical line (semicolon-joined assignments in team_stats/standings/statistics); maintainability=0.256 in scores.json.
suggestion: Split compound statements onto separate lines for readability; behaviour is unaffected.
